# RenderContext

<!-- Generated from the doc comments in the library. Do not edit this file. -->

Carries page, canvas, resource, navigation, tagging, and cursor state through layout.

Import from `@bonniepdf/core`. Implements `RenderContextContract`.

## Constructors

```typescript
new RenderContext()
```

### `ambientHorizontalTextAlignment`

```typescript
ambientHorizontalTextAlignment: TextAlignment | undefined
```

The horizontal text alignment a Container establishes for descendant text (TextBlock/Heading/RichText) that sets none of its own, cascading through nesting the way CSS text-align is inherited. `undefined` means no ambient is in effect: unset text stays at its own default (Left). Scoped to the container's subtree by the container itself, which restores the value it found on the way in.

### `canvas`

```typescript
canvas: ICanvas
```

The canvas that elements currently draw onto.

### `cellStretchHeight`

```typescript
cellStretchHeight: number
```

The height `cellStretchTarget` fills: the row height less the cell's padding.

### `cellStretchTarget`

```typescript
cellStretchTarget: Container | undefined
```

While a table draws a cell whose content is a `Container` (seen through pass-through wrappers), that container. It fills `cellStretchHeight`, so a border or background applied to a cell's content spans the whole row rather than only the cell's own text. `undefined` everywhere else; no other container is affected.

### `chromeReservationSuspended`

```typescript
chromeReservationSuspended: boolean
```

While true, `contentTop` and `maxY` ignore the chrome reservation. Set only while the engine paints the chrome itself: a header is not laid out inside the band it reserves for the body.

### `contentBottom`

```typescript
readonly contentBottom: number
```

*read-only*

Bottom of the body content band: `pageHeight - max(margin, footerHeight)`.

### `contentHeight`

```typescript
readonly contentHeight: number
```

*read-only*

Usable body height on the current page: the full content band, not just what is left below the cursor. Elements use it to ask "would this fit on a fresh page at all?" before deciding to break rather than split.

### `contentTop`

```typescript
readonly contentTop: number
```

*read-only*

Top of the body content band: `max(margin, headerHeight)`. Chrome that fits inside the top margin reserves nothing beyond the margin the page already had, so this reduces to `margin` for the overwhelming majority of documents.

### `flushExternalCanvas`

```typescript
flushExternalCanvas(canvas: ICanvas): void
```

Flushes an externally-created canvas (e.g. from getCanvas) into the *currently active* canvas (`this.canvas`) - not directly into `pages[currentPageIndex]`. Necessary for chart elements that draw to a positioned canvas rather than ctx.canvas.

This distinction matters whenever `this.canvas` is not the page's own live canvas - most notably the fixed canvas a page background/foreground slot renders into (see `PdfRenderPipeline.renderPageSlotElement`), which accumulates its own operators separately and is prepended/appended to the page stream only after the slot element finishes rendering. A chart or `CanvasElement` used as that slot's content calls `getCanvas()` to get a positioned child canvas, exactly like any other caller of this method; if this method wrote straight into `pages[]`, that write would land immediately - ahead of the slot's own prepend/append step, and outside the fixed canvas entirely, so the slot's rendered background would land in the wrong place in the painter's-model order (observed: a `CanvasElement` used as `pageBackground` painted over already-rendered page content instead of behind it, in PDF output only - SVG export writes into `this.canvas` already, via `appendRawMarkup` below, so it never exhibited the bug). Writing into `this.canvas`'s own stream keeps this method's PDF behaviour symmetric with its SVG branch: both append into whatever canvas is currently active, letting the caller (ordinary page rendering, or a slot's fixed-canvas redirect) decide where that ends up.

### `refreshChromeReservation`

```typescript
refreshChromeReservation(): void
```

Re-measures the current page's chrome. Called on every page switch and on every page break; the pipelines also call it directly after assigning a new page size or margin, because those change the width the chrome is measured against.
